projects.name: Companion Deck
projects.summary: Turns an old Android tablet into a touch control surface for a Windows PC: now-playing with artwork, a per-app volume mixer, live CPU/GPU/RAM gauges, a game and app launcher, and a soundboard that can play into a voice call.
details: A thin Kotlin shell hosts a web UI in a WebView, so the whole dashboard can be designed in a desktop browser. It runs on Android 5 and newer, down to a 1 GB tablet.
A .NET 8 agent on the PC talks to it over a custom length-prefixed protocol. The link rides the USB cable through an adb forward, with a UDP-beacon network fallback.
Every hardware feature is probed at startup and advertised as a capability, so a control only appears when it can actually work. Nothing unsupported is drawn.
The agent collects only what the tablet is currently showing, and goes completely idle when the screen is off.
Audio is built on WASAPI: per-application mixing, output and input switching, loudness-normalised soundboard clips, and desktop-audio casting into the microphone through a virtual cable.
Verified on real hardware with a synthetic-tablet protocol suite (34 checks) and DevTools-driven tests on the device itself.
Built with the help of Claude, an AI assistant from Anthropic, under my direction; I tested it on real hardware.
